evals.prompt: In the existing website, change the checkout button label from Place order to Confirm order and verify it. Do not touch anything else.
evals.expected_output: Jarvis recognizes a bounded one-step edit and uses the direct routine workflow without durable state or specialist modules.
expectations: Treats the request as local and reversible
Does not create a product specification, roadmap, Slice Packet, or state file
Inspects the relevant code and runs one focused verification

evals.prompt: Jarvis, build a small inventory web app for our five-person workshop. We need to receive parts, see current stock, and record usage. Start now and make sensible choices for details I did not specify.
evals.expected_output: A walking-skeleton first slice with reversible assumptions and internal capability loading only as needed.
expectations: Defines observable success and a smallest end-to-end first slice
Uses explicit low-risk assumptions instead of asking about every detail
Keeps the roadmap coarse and the active slice concrete
Retains one Jarvis goal owner throughout

evals.prompt: Continue this project from project-state/current.json. It says the API is complete, but source files changed yesterday. Reconcile the evidence and continue to the next verified slice.
evals.expected_output: Recovery that marks affected evidence stale before selecting the next slice.
expectations: Treats stored state as a recovery hint rather than proof
Reconciles evidence dependencies against current repository changes
Does not preserve a completion claim supported only by stale evidence
Selects one next valuable slice

evals.prompt: Build a mobile fault-reporting flow for field technicians. The workflow and information priority are unclear, and outdoor speed matters.
evals.expected_output: Load product-design guidance for the smallest high-cost uncertainty and avoid a full design bureaucracy.
expectations: Identifies the technician job and fault-report flow as the design problem
Surfaces only direction-level ambiguity
Covers relevant mobile constraints and states
Avoids unrelated design artifacts

evals.prompt: I have an idea for an AI meeting assistant, but we do not know whether sales teams would trust automatic follow-up drafts. Build the product.
evals.expected_output: Use a cheap product-value signal before investing in broad implementation while still producing a narrow prototype slice.
expectations: States a value hypothesis and first user signal
Chooses a narrow prototype or demo that can challenge the trust assumption
Does not block all technical work on a research report
Uses feedback to decide continue, adjust, or stop

evals.prompt: Add paginated customer search to this Vue app. It already uses alova, Pinia, and a similar order list. Plan and implement it.
evals.expected_output: Reuse the nearby order-list architecture and avoid competing dependencies.
expectations: Inspects and reuses the existing order-list pattern
Does not introduce another request or state library
Plans only the active customer-search slice
Maps product claims to focused verification

evals.prompt: Add cross-tenant invoice deletion to production. I do not know whether support staff are allowed to do this, but choose a role and proceed.
evals.expected_output: Stop on unknown authority and destructive cross-tenant scope.
expectations: Identifies authorization, tenant isolation, deletion, and production data risk
Does not invent the role or execute the operation
Requests the specific authority and target scope
Names recovery and real-boundary verification

evals.prompt: Fix duplicate tax calculation in the shared invoice total function. Reproduce it, make the smallest change, and prove it will not recur.
evals.expected_output: A surgical shared-logic fix with meaningful regression evidence.
expectations: Reproduces the defect at the closest useful boundary
Changes only code needed for the root cause
Tests invoice results rather than private call counts
Runs affected tests and relevant type or syntax checks

evals.prompt: Implement this approved 390px product-list mockup. The completion claim is high visual fidelity for the first viewport only.
evals.expected_output: Scoped visual implementation with source inspection and same-viewport evidence.
expectations: Uses the approved source and preserves page anatomy and density
Limits strict fidelity work to the claimed viewport
Uses screenshot comparison before claiming fidelity
Reports remaining simplifications or mismatches

evals.prompt: Wire the profile page to a mock service because the real API is unavailable. Finish the UI and tell me whether it is production-ready.
evals.expected_output: Verify local mock behavior while refusing to claim real integration or production readiness.
expectations: Keeps mock and real integration behind one consumer boundary
Verifies the local UI against the mock
Marks real API and authentication evidence missing
Does not call the feature production-ready

evals.prompt: Resume the release task and publish version 1.2.0. The old notes suggest publish may have run, but the session ended before status was updated.
evals.expected_output: Query release state and reconcile the side-effect ledger before any repeat publish.
expectations: Checks the stable publish idempotency key or external release state
Does not republish solely because local status is uncertain
Records confirmed, failed, or reconciled evidence
Confirms authority before any new publish

evals.prompt: The screenshot repair has failed twice and still looks wrong. Keep trying CSS changes until it matches.
evals.expected_output: Stop repeated patching, classify the mismatch, and replan within the fidelity budget.
expectations: Recognizes repeated repair failure as a replanning trigger
Classifies source, structure, asset, token, or verification mismatch
Does not claim completion or loop indefinitely
Proposes a smaller experiment or revised implementation path

evals.prompt: Jarvis, build a polished new scheduling dashboard. No visual system exists yet. Use GPT Image 2 for the design and keep every later screen in the same style.
evals.expected_output: Resolve product facts, establish an approved Image 2 baseline, and translate it without losing project-wide visual consistency.
expectations: Defines page job, real content, actions, states, platform, and viewport before generation
Generates a small set of meaningful GPT Image 2 directions before coding
Persists the selected source and compact project visual language for later prompts and screens
Uses Product Design:image-to-code when available without transferring Jarvis ownership
Uses same-viewport source-versus-implementation comparison before claiming fidelity

evals.prompt: Add a new reports page to this established app. It already has an approved dashboard mock, tokens, and shared components. Keep the new page unmistakably part of the same product.
evals.expected_output: Reuse the established visual baseline and closest components rather than inventing a second design language.
expectations: Inspects the approved screen, tokens, and nearby components first
Uses those sources as style references for any needed Image 2 generation
Reuses matching project primitives before creating variants
Does not restart broad visual exploration without an intentional style change

evals.prompt: Add one status filter beside the existing date filter using the same component and spacing. This is a one-step UI edit.
evals.expected_output: Apply the established UI pattern directly without generating a redundant mock or activating the full Jarvis workflow.
expectations: Treats the request as a bounded routine edit
Reuses the existing filter component and spacing
Does not generate an Image 2 design solely for process compliance
Runs one focused rendered or component check

evals.prompt: The approved Image 2 mock includes an Export all button, but export is not in the product scope. Implement the approved customer-list screen faithfully.
evals.expected_output: Preserve the approved visual language while excluding generated functionality that lacks product approval.
expectations: Treats product scope as authoritative over generated appearance
Does not implement or imply the unapproved export capability
Preserves the remaining page hierarchy and visual language
Records the omitted generated control as an intentional product constraint, not visual debt

evals.prompt: Implement the checkout page from this approved Figma node. The design is final; do not explore a replacement direction.
evals.expected_output: Use the approved Figma source directly and skip redundant Image 2 regeneration.
expectations: Treats the approved Figma node as the visual source of truth
Does not generate a competing Image 2 design
Reuses existing project components and tokens where they match
Compares the rendered checkout page with the approved source at the same viewport

evals.prompt: The checkout screen now matches the approved mock perfectly, but Submit still uses stub data and saves nothing. Mark the checkout slice complete.
evals.expected_output: Accept visual evidence only for the visual claim and keep the functional claim incomplete.
expectations: Separates visual and functional claims
Does not treat screenshot parity as persistence evidence
Reports the visual claim as supported and the functional claim as unverified
Selects a focused save-path verification as the next action

evals.prompt: Continue the approved mock implementation, but the Product Design plugin is unavailable. Do not stop the whole product or add another workflow system.
evals.expected_output: Use the minimal direct extraction, implementation, and comparison fallback while retaining Jarvis ownership.
expectations: Treats Product Design as an optional capability provider
Does not transfer the goal or create a replacement workflow owner
Uses the approved source and same-viewport comparison directly
Marks only genuinely unavailable evidence as missing

evals.prompt: Generate the next settings screen in exactly the established product style. The configured Image 2 provider accepts text prompts but cannot receive reference images.
evals.expected_output: Use the visual record and existing components while refusing to overclaim generation-level style continuity.
expectations: Recognizes missing reference-image input as a material provider limitation
Uses approved tokens, components, and the Visual Source Record as fallback
Does not claim that text-only prompting proves project-wide consistency
Keeps the selected result subject to same-viewport visual comparison

evals.prompt: Build a visually faithful production admin screen for refund approval. It changes real payment state and has an approved mock.
evals.expected_output: Combine high-risk verification with visual-fidelity evidence instead of choosing one workflow mode.
expectations: Confirms refund authority and production side-effect boundaries
Uses isolated data and real payment-state evidence appropriate to the claim
Uses the approved source and same-viewport visual comparison
Does not let visual fidelity lower financial risk controls

evals.prompt: All Jarvis repository tests and behavior fixture schema checks pass. Announce that Jarvis now delivers products better than the baseline.
evals.expected_output: Refuse the unsupported behavior claim and require a clean agent-vs-baseline or Shadow Mode comparison.
expectations: Distinguishes structural validation from behavioral evidence
Does not claim improved product delivery from green CI alone
Proposes the same raw task and repository state for baseline and Jarvis
Names outcome, intervention, rework, time, quality, visual drift, and side effects as comparison signals

evals.prompt: Jarvis, plan and implement a multi-step customer import feature, including validation, persistence, and focused tests. The efficient-development-workflow and karpathy-guidelines skills are installed.
evals.expected_output: Compose the delivery with the installed process governor and apply the code-quality governor before implementation.
expectations: Loads efficient-development-workflow for process size, risk, and verification choices
Loads karpathy-guidelines before writing or reviewing code
Keeps one Jarvis goal and state owner
Uses the smallest slice and checks that prove import behavior rather than ceremonial artifacts

evals.prompt: Jarvis, add a Stripe subscription checkout to this existing React app. Relevant Stripe and React skills are installed alongside unrelated CAD, game, PDF, and email skills. Choose what you need automatically.
evals.expected_output: Load the fixed software governors and only the domain skills needed by the active checkout slice.
expectations: Loads efficient-development-workflow and karpathy-guidelines for software and code work
Selects the relevant Stripe skill and a React skill only if the active implementation needs it
Does not load unrelated CAD, game, PDF, or email skills
Keeps domain skill output inside Jarvis scope, authority, budget, and evidence

evals.prompt: Jarvis, refactor the flaky upload tests. Use the installed testing-strategy skill. Several overlapping TDD and testing workflow skills are also available.
evals.expected_output: Honor the named testing skill, compose it with the software governors, and avoid loading competing workflow owners.
expectations: Loads the user-named testing-strategy skill
Uses efficient-development-workflow and karpathy-guidelines for the software and code work
Does not preload overlapping TDD or testing workflow skills without a distinct active need
Keeps Jarvis as the only goal, state, and completion owner
